knitr::opts_chunk$set(

`create_NICHESObject()` needs an expression matrix, cell metadata and an LR
database. This guide shows how to prepare each one.

```{r load}
library(NICHESv2)
data(NICHESv2_inputs)
```

## Expression matrix

`count.mtx` is a gene-by-cell matrix, sparse or dense. Row names are gene symbols
and column names are cell barcodes.

```{r matrix}
class(NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx)
dim(NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx)
```

The values you pass set what the scores mean. Raw counts give absolute
magnitudes, and normalized expression gives relative scores. NICHESv2 uses the
matrix as it is, so this choice affects which edges score highest.

## Cell metadata

`meta.data` is a data frame with cell barcodes as row names, matching the matrix
columns. What else it needs depends on the mode:

| Mode | Required columns |
|---|---|
| `"spatial"` | `x` and `y` |
| `"nonspatial"` | the column named by `cell.type.col` |

Other columns carry through to `$cell.meta` and appear on each edge in
`$edge.meta`.

```{r meta}
head(NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data, 3)
```

### Several samples

When your data has several samples, set `sample.col` to the column that identifies
them. Each sample is processed separately and the results are merged, so no edges
cross samples.

Barcodes must be unique across all samples, and a duplicate stops the merge with
an error. Add a prefix first if needed, such as
`paste0(sample.id, "_", barcode)`.

## LR databases

Pass one of three database names to `LRM.db`, or your own data frame.

| Name | Species | Needs internet |
|---|---|---|
| `"connectomedb2025"` | human, mouse, rat, pig | No |
| `"fantom5"` | human, mouse, rat, pig | No |
| `"omnipath"` | human, mouse, rat | Yes, plus OmnipathR |

`create_NICHESObject()` has no default database, so always set `LRM.db`. Set
`species` to match your data. To look at a database first:

```{r database}
db <- load_LRM_database("connectomedb2025", species = "mouse", verbose = FALSE)
nrow(db)
head(db[, c("ligand", "receptor")], 3)
```

### Your own database

A custom data frame needs ligand and receptor columns. If they have other names,
set `ligand.col` and `receptor.col`. Multi-gene complexes are written with
underscores, and a pair is dropped if any of its genes is missing from the matrix.

```{r custom}
my.db <- data.frame(
  L = c("Gene1", "Gene3"),
  R = c("Gene2", "Gene4_Gene5")
)
obj <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx    = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  meta.data    = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data,
  LRM.db       = my.db,
  ligand.col   = "L",
  receptor.col = "R",
  mode         = "spatial",
  k            = 5L,
  verbose      = FALSE
)
obj$LRM.list
```

## Seurat objects

`extract_NICHESInputs_Seurat()` needs the SeuratObject package and reads both V4
and V5 objects, so you don't need to update an older object first. It returns
`count.mtx` and `meta.data`.

```{r seurat, eval = requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE)}
seu <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(
  counts    = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  meta.data = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data
)
inputs <- extract_NICHESInputs_Seurat(
  seu, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts", verbose = FALSE
)
dim(inputs$count.mtx)
```

Spatial coordinates aren't copied automatically, because Seurat keeps them with
the image. For spatial objects, add them yourself, as shown in the
[spatial tutorial](spatial-tutorial.html):

```{r seurat-coords, eval = FALSE}
coords <- SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates(seurat.obj)
inputs$meta.data$x <- coords[rownames(inputs$meta.data), "x"]
inputs$meta.data$y <- coords[rownames(inputs$meta.data), "y"]
```

## AnnData files

`extract_NICHESInputs_AnnData()` reads `.h5ad` files through the rhdf5 package, so
Python isn't needed. `layer = "counts"` reads the counts layer, and `obs.cols`
limits which metadata columns are kept.

```{r anndata, eval = requireNamespace("rhdf5", quietly = TRUE)}
h5ad <- system.file("extdata", "NICHESv2_example.h5ad", package = "NICHESv2")
inputs <- extract_NICHESInputs_AnnData(h5ad, layer = "counts", verbose = FALSE)
dim(inputs$count.mtx)
colnames(inputs$meta.data)
```

Install rhdf5 from Bioconductor:

```{r rhdf5, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("rhdf5")
```
